text:
nina: heads-up — Brightleaf tenant is totally blocked after the RBAC role mapping refactor we ran at 17:02. They get 403 on model calls and billing pages. tenant: brightleaf-prod. error shows: `403 missing permission: models.invoke`

alex: which rollout exactly? the squash-service-roles change? any rollout id or req id?

nina: yes, we flipped squash-service-roles=true during the refactor. req id from their failing request: req_0a1b2c3d. snippet from api gateway: 
```
{"ts":"2026-03-20T17:07:12Z","req_id":"req_0a1b2c3d","user":"brightleaf:user-anna","resource":"models.invoke","err":"403 Forbidden - missing permission"}
```

jamal: digging into traces — I see KMS decrypt failures for the tenant service key around the same time: `AccessDenied: iam:Decrypt` on key `projects/redwood/keys/brightleaf-key`. If the model key fails to unwrap we fall back into denied states and RBAC checks can cascade.

rita: CSM reported customer is blocked from billing UI and needs access to close end-of-month invoices. Customer is escalated and asking for a quick workaround.

maria: don't grant org-admin wide. Recommend a minimal temporary grant to the tenant service principal: `roles/model-invoke` + `roles/billing-view` for 30m. We'll roll that back once we confirm.

alex: agree with maria. Also need the audit entry for the refactor so we can see which mapping removed `models.invoke` from their service principal. Query I ran: `SELECT * FROM rbac_audit WHERE change_type='mapping_sweep' AND cluster='prod' AND ts > '2026-03-20T16:50:00Z'`

nina: I can run the support action now to add the two roles temporarily. executing `support-grant --tenant brightleaf-prod --roles model-invoke,billing-view --ttl 30m --reason "blocker SR-5972"`

ops-bot: support action executed by nina: grant roles [model-invoke,billing-view] to principal brightleaf:service-main (ttl=30m). ticket=SR-5972.

nina: customer confirms — billing page loads and model calls succeed from their side. :white_check_mark:

alex: I found the mapping change in the rollout: the attribute filter `service==true` was merged into the new squash rule and inadvertently removed `models.invoke` from principals that only matched on legacy attributes. I'll open a revert PR and a migration test. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/rbac/changes/5622

maria: follow-up: add a canary test to the deploy pipeline to call `models.invoke` and `billing.view` for a sample tenant after mapping changes. Also add an alert on KMS `Decrypt` AccessDenied spikes.

jamal: KMS team applied a binding fix for the Brightleaf key — they added the service account back to the key ACL. I've attached the minimal ACL diff to the ticket.

nina: closing SR-5972 with temporary grant revoked (ops-bot shows revoke at +30m). Customer verified access persists after revoke. Leaving follow-up tasks in the ticket: (1) revert mapping change, (2) add canary test, (3) KMS ACL audit.

alex: I'll handle the revert PR and include migration and test notes. tagging @maria for pipeline changes.

rita: told CSM + customer the plan and timeline. they're ok with the revert approach.

ops-bot: ticket SR-5972 status=resolved, actions=[grant_roles, revoke_roles], notes="temporary grant; revert PR opened: 5622"

nina: thanks all. logging this for postmortem and to include in the next security runbook. :lock:
